title: Multi-step workflow — zero-downtime datatype change on a large table
migration_snippet:
# Goal: change orders.created_at from DATE to TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE on a
#       20M-row table, with no downtime.
# Current: app reads and writes orders.created_at as DATE
# Constraint: a direct ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY is rejected (ORA-01439) because
#             changing datatype class requires an empty column.
expected_feedback: Workflow: this is a datatype class change, so a direct ALTER TABLE MODIFY fails with ORA-01439 no matter how large the maintenance window — the driver is rejection, not duration. On EE use DBMS_REDEFINITION: (1) CAN_REDEF_TABLE with CONS_USE_PK, (2) create the interim table with the new schema, (3) START_REDEF_TABLE with a col_mapping CAST, (4) COPY_TABLE_DEPENDENTS and check num_errors, gating on DBA_REDEFINITION_ERRORS, (5) SYNC_INTERIM_TABLE, (6) FINISH_REDEF_TABLE with an explicit dml_lock_timeout for the brief atomic swap, (7) verify the dependent-object inventory matches, then cleanup and DBMS_STATS. Rollback before step 6 is abort-before-cutover via ABORT_REDEF_TABLE plus dropping the interim table; after step 6 it is restore/PITR. On Standard Edition DBMS_REDEFINITION is unavailable and the only path is CTAS plus a quiesced two-step cutover in a maintenance window.
